# Recreation Prompt

Recreate `Rain-Kissed Covenant`, a portrait-first browser interactive novel about a mortal teenager meeting Rowan, an obviously immortal transfer student, in a rain-soaked pine clearing. Preserve the source mechanics exactly: start screen, tap-to-advance typewriter dialogue, three choice gates with score deltas, Yearning meter starting at 50, four threshold endings, restart/menu, and mobile pointer/click controls. Rebuild the presentation as a satirical forbidden romance fantasy with moody forests, crescent moon, rain, fireflies, love-triangle jokes, gothic locket UI, readable bottom dialogue, compact top HUD, and catalog-backed forest audio/approved feedback GIF accents. Use inline HTML/CSS/JS, Canvas for procedural atmosphere and the focal immortal portrait, and avoid changing scoring or progression semantics.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint — Rain-Kissed Covenant

## Source game truth
The preserved source (`index_old.html`) is an interactive visual novel. It starts on a title screen, then uses a canvas ambience, typewriter dialogue, tap-to-continue, three branching choice sets, score deltas, and four score-threshold endings. The core objective is to choose responses that keep the relationship score high enough for better endings.

## Protected mechanics
- Start button enters the story.
- Dialogue appears with typewriter timing and can be tapped to complete.
- Non-choice dialogue advances on tap.
- Choice nodes present three options.
- Affection starts at 50 and changes by the same style of positive/neutral/negative deltas.
- Endings are selected by thresholds: 75+, 40+, 10+, below 10.
- Restart replays the same language/session; menu returns to the title.
- Audio is only initiated after user gesture and failures are nonblocking.

## Rebuilt target
The canonical `index.html` reinterprets the same mechanics as a satirical forbidden romance fantasy: the relationship score is Yearning, the caller is Rowan the immortal transfer student, and the branching conversation occurs in a rainy supernatural forest. Presentation is rebuilt with procedural Canvas/CSS rather than relying on the previous neon city image.

## Safe transformation surfaces
Copy, title, HUD vocabulary, fonts, colors, canvas background, focal character drawing, audio URLs from catalog, GIF feedback, buttons, and responsive UI styling are safe to transform because they do not alter the branching/scoring semantics.
